cohort: The study included 393 pregnant women, consisting of 131 cases who received pharmacological obstetric analgesia and 262 controls who did not.
finding: Pharmacological obstetric analgesia was associated with an increased risk for the use of exogenous oxytocin, episiotomy, Kristeller maneuver, forceps, and lower first-minute Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Pharmacological analgesia increased the risk of episiotomy, Kristeller maneuver, and forceps, but did not increase the risk of spontaneous perineal tear or abdominal delivery.
